title: Dockerize Your Application
implemented: Multi-stage, non-root platform images around the original pinned DataScientest application; digest-pinned Alpine backend, health checks and a reviewed dependency patch.
tested: Sequential builds and authenticated application tests passed. Secure release db2efa8 was published to GHCR; both public SHA tags returned anonymous HTTP 200 and their digests matched actual running Kubernetes pods. Frontend and authenticated API routing through Traefik passed. On 2026-10-24, ef41449 images were verified anonymously and their digests matched actual dev and prod pods.
gaps: Public/cloud availability and externally trusted ingress/TLS remain untested. Both local environments have now run the verified release.
engineering: I can package an existing application reproducibly and validate the complete UI–API–database path.

title: Deploy the Application in Multiple Environments (Dev & Prod)
implemented: Separate dev/prod namespaces, ConfigMaps, credential objects, PostgreSQL/PVCs and deployment policies. Production now pins verified GHCR digests; migration init-container uses the same backend digest. Dev SHA tag matches latest verified automatic promotion.
tested: Both current overlays were deployed sequentially on real k3s. All pods/rollouts/PVCs became Ready; frontend, health, database readiness, browser login and authenticated CRUD passed. Both directions of cross-namespace database, credential and record isolation passed; dev was rechecked after prod. Registry digests matched both runtimes.
gaps: PASSED scope is sequential local deployment through loopback service port-forwards and a temporary proxy. Concurrent full stacks, public DNS/TLS, cloud deployment and canonical production Argo manual sync remain NOT YET TESTED. Dev auto-sync and prod manual-main policies are unchanged.
engineering: I separate configuration and release policies while being explicit about shared-node failure domains.

title: Run Tests on the Application
implemented: Upstream tests, PostgreSQL migrations, mypy/Ruff, and metrics/readiness checks run in CI.
tested: 55 upstream tests and 2 platform tests pass; exact CI script passes locally and hosted backend-tests/lint jobs passed at 211199d. New browser login/create/reload smoke passed. Current main ef41449 and PR18 application workflows passed; fresh dev/prod HTTP/login/CRUD and browser checks passed.
gaps: The complete automated browser E2E suite and OpenAPI-client regeneration are NOT YET TESTED.
engineering: I use automated checks and a focused functional smoke test to catch compatibility regressions.

title: Container Orchestration with Kubernetes
implemented: Deployments, StatefulSet, PVC, Services, ConfigMap, Ingress, namespace policy and resource/security settings.
tested: Current hardened dev: Ready k3s node, all three pods 1/1, Deployments/StatefulSet ready, 8 GiB PVC Bound, healthy Ingress, authenticated Traefik routing, real image pulls, Argo reconciliation and Git-revert rollout passed. On 2026-10-24 both current dev/prod overlays ran sequentially with three Ready pods each, independent storage and matching published images. Cross-namespace DB rejection and positive controls passed in both directions.
gaps: Hetzner orchestration, concurrent full web stacks and additional NetworkPolicy paths (arbitrary clients, ingress/monitoring) remain NOT YET TESTED. Temporary clusters were removed after capture.
engineering: I translate application dependencies into orchestrated resources and verify readiness, storage and routing.

title: Automate Deployment (CI/CD Pipeline)
implemented: Tests/build/strict-scan gates, exact-scanned-image publication, guarded dev promotion, automatic Argo dev reconciliation and manual production sync policy.
tested: Main db2efa8 passed scans and publication; its promotion failed on a generated-tag merge conflict. The reviewed helper recovered real deploy/dev at 1b0ffd5 and three Git regression tests passed. Argo reached exact-revision Synced/Healthy/Succeeded from public GitHub with real GHCR images; an isolated Git revert restored the prior template and ReplicaSet. Later main ef41449 workflow 39939061134 passed every job, including tests, strict scans, image publication and dev promotion. Both local overlays ran the published pair; production was explicitly applied with kubectl.
gaps: Canonical production Argo manual synchronization is NOT YET TESTED. The new guarded helper in open PR18 still needs hosted main execution after merge; the latest successful main promotion used the existing workflow. Production pins need review/merge to main before canonical GitOps deployment.
engineering: I design a delivery chain that blocks unsafe releases and keep Git promotion distinct from successful deployment.

title: Create IaC (Infrastructure as Code) Templates
implemented: Terraform Hetzner templates and Ansible preparation/k3s/kubeconfig playbooks, with restricted SSH configuration.
tested: Fresh Terraform fmt/validate and three Ansible syntax checks passed; hosted platform validation passed.
gaps: Terraform plan/apply, actual remote provisioning and server recreation are NOT YET TESTED. No Hetzner API resources were created.
engineering: I express infrastructure as reviewed code and validate it before any billable provisioning.

title: Monitor the Application
implemented: Prometheus/Grafana resources, FastAPI metrics, dashboard, ServiceMonitor and unavailable/5xx alert rules.
tested: All three isolated targets were UP including Grafana; real synthetic request/rate/latency/error metrics rendered; the one-minute unavailable alert fired and cleared after recovery.
gaps: The new ServiceMonitor discovery in Kubernetes, receiver delivery, sustained 5xx alert scenario and durable monitoring recovery are NOT YET TESTED.
engineering: I instrument service behavior and validate alert evaluation rather than equating process uptime with observability.

title: Think About Security (DevSecOps)
implemented: Dependency remediation, strict source/image gates, non-root/read-only controls, dropped capabilities, NetworkPolicies and safe temporary credential cleanup.
tested: Backend reached 0 HIGH/CRITICAL locally and passed hosted strict image scanning at db2efa8 before publication. Source/configuration gates passed. Current non-root/read-only/drop-all Kubernetes workloads ran successfully. Public Git/GHCR needed no repository or registry credential; obsolete public imagePullSecrets references were removed and tested on the isolated branch. On 2026-10-24 both environments ran with existing hardened contexts and distinct credentials; positive own-DB and negative cross-namespace DB controls passed.
gaps: Additional NetworkPolicy paths, public DNS/TLS and cloud production security remain NOT YET TESTED. Database cross-namespace rejection is verified; this does not prove every traffic policy.
engineering: I quantify security improvement, keep failing policy checks enabled, and distinguish configuration from enforcement.

title: Think About Disaster Recovery
implemented: Atomic compressed PostgreSQL backups, recovery/rollback runbooks and off-node snapshot/token guidance.
tested: PG16 backup/restore and failed-dump cleanup previously passed. A real public-GitHub controlled rollout followed by Git revert returned Argo to Synced/Healthy, restored the exact backend template hash and ReplicaSet, and preserved the same API/database record after both rollouts.
gaps: Image-version/schema downgrade, actual k3s snapshot/restore, off-site durability and replacement-server/cloud recovery are NOT YET TESTED. The earlier database backup used its documented kubectl-to-Docker adapter; the new GitOps rollback used real Kubernetes and Argo.
engineering: I prove recovery with restored data and failure-path checks while stating the boundary of the drill.

title: Documentation
implemented: Architecture/runbooks, exact ten-heading compliance mapping, provenance-backed screenshot index, capture protocol and both ten-minute plans.
tested: All 51 earlier screenshot hashes/bytes preserved; 11 new genuine captures, dated source provenance, paths, offline gallery and both 600-second demonstration plans checked. Updated deployment/results distinguish local production runtime from public/cloud readiness.
gaps: The architecture is a design view; future cloud boxes are not deployment evidence. This is an evidence pack, not an exported PowerPoint deck.
engineering: I make the system reviewable and explain its tested capabilities and remaining risks precisely.
